title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 48 (Variation of Shareholders’ Rights)

content.overview: Section 48(1) provides that where the share capital of a company is divided into different classes of shares, the rights attached to the shares of any class may be varied with the consent in writing of the holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class or by means of a special resolution passed at a separate meeting of the holders of the issued shares of that class—(a) if provision with respect to such variation is contained in the memorandum or articles of the company; or (b) in the absence of any such provision in the memorandum or articles, if such variation is not prohibited by the terms of issue of the shares of that class. Provided that if variation by one class of shareholders affects the rights of any other class of shareholders, the consent of three-fourths of such other class of shareholders shall also be obtained and the provisions of this section shall apply to such variation. Section 48(2) provides that where the holders of not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of a class did not consent to such variation or vote in favour of the special resolution for the variation, they may apply to the Tribunal to have the variation cancelled, and where any such application is made, the variation shall not have effect unless and until it is confirmed by the Tribunal. An application under this section shall be made within twenty-one days after the date on which the consent was given or the resolution was passed, as the case may be, and may be made on behalf of the shareholders entitled to make the application by such one or more of their number as they may appoint in writing for the purpose. The decision of the Tribunal on any application under sub-section (2) shall be binding on the shareholders. The company shall, within thirty days of the date of the order of the Tribunal, file a copy thereof with the Registrar.
content.glance: Class rights varied by 3/4 written consent or class special resolution (if memo/articles allow or terms of issue do not prohibit); if variation affects another class, 3/4 of that class also; ≥10% dissenters may apply to Tribunal within 21 days; variation ineffective until Tribunal confirms; Tribunal decision binding; file order with Registrar within 30 days.
content.study: Where share capital is divided into different classes, rights of any class may be varied with written consent of holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class, or by special resolution at a separate meeting of holders of that class, if the memorandum or articles so provide, or if there is no such provision, if the variation is not prohibited by the terms of issue (s. 48(1)). If variation by one class affects rights of another class, three-fourths consent of that other class is also required. Holders of not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of a class who did not consent or vote in favour may apply to the Tribunal within twenty-one days to have the variation cancelled; the variation does not take effect unless and until confirmed by the Tribunal (s. 48(2)). Tribunal decision is binding; company must file a copy of the order with the Registrar within thirty days. Current-law framing: identify class and proposed variation; test memo/articles or terms of issue; apply 3/4 mechanism and other-class proviso; note 10% dissenters’ 21-day Tribunal route and filing duty.

sections.heading: Variation mechanism (s. 48(1))
sections.body: Written consent of holders of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of the class, or special resolution at a separate class meeting, where the memorandum or articles provide for variation, or where there is no such provision and the variation is not prohibited by the terms of issue.

sections.heading: Other class affected
sections.body: If variation by one class affects the rights of any other class, consent of three-fourths of such other class is also required.

sections.heading: Dissenters’ application (s. 48(2))
sections.body: Holders of not less than ten per cent of the issued shares of the class who did not consent or vote in favour may apply to the Tribunal within twenty-one days to cancel the variation. The variation does not take effect unless and until confirmed by the Tribunal.

sections.heading: Tribunal order and filing
sections.body: Tribunal decision is binding on the shareholders. The company shall file a copy of the order with the Registrar within thirty days of the date of the order.

examples.title: Class special resolution
examples.body: Preference shareholders pass a special resolution at a separate meeting to alter preferential dividend rights (memo/articles allow). Section 48 is engaged; dissenters with ≥10% may apply to the Tribunal within 21 days.

examples.title: Affecting another class
examples.body: Variation of equity rights affects preference rights. Consent of three-fourths of preference holders is also required under the proviso to s. 48(1).

hypotheticals.question: Is a simple majority of the class enough to vary class rights?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 48 requires written consent of not less than three-fourths of the issued shares of that class, or a special resolution at a separate class meeting.

hypotheticals.question: When must dissenters apply to the Tribunal?
hypotheticals.analysis: Within twenty-one days after the date on which the consent was given or the resolution was passed.

distinctions.title: Variation of rights (s. 48) vs voting rights (s. 47)
distinctions.left: How class rights may be changed and challenged
distinctions.right: Who votes on resolutions in the ordinary course

misconceptions.trap: Any board resolution can vary class rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 48 requires class consent (3/4) or class special resolution, with a Tribunal route for qualifying dissenters within 21 days.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 48 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify class and proposed variation. II. Test memo/articles or terms of issue. III. Apply 3/4 consent or class SR; other-class proviso if relevant. IV. Note ≥10% dissenters’ 21-day Tribunal route. V. Filing of Tribunal order. VI. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Class; variation; consent/resolution compliance; other-class impact; dissenters’ standing and timing; precise relief.
